threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still stop at the red pedestrian lights, not realizing they’re optional after midnight. It’s a rite of passage, really.
Last night on the 3 bus, a guy was singing opera to a bemused crowd. Not one person moved, we were all too intrigued by his dedication.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy strumming a guitar at Hermannplatz, while two kids played football between the buses. That's Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find spontaneous street parties on a Tuesday night, complete with karaoke and a vegan curry stand. It's a vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you’re local when you can name at least three places that have a better burrito than La Taqueria, and you’ve argued about it too.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today that stopped for a street performer’s solo on the corner. Everyone clapped, then the bus driver just shook his head and drove off.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the parks are for lounging, but locals sprint through them to dodge the crowds and grab a quick coffee before work.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they still walk around clutching a map, stopping to snap pics of every building, while locals just breeze past.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot newcomers by how they carry their coffee—always in that Instagrammable cup, not realizing you just grab any old mug at the local café.
Last night on the 35, a guy serenaded us with a ukulele cover of 'Wonderwall' while the bus lurched through Brixton. Best terrible moment ever.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The smell of fresh döner wafting through the air during late-night strolls—felt like home when I saw the same old guy in the shop at 3 AM.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you enjoy a kebab at 3 AM, served with a side of graffiti art that tells stories of protests and community love.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they refuse to wait in line for brunch but hop right into the taco truck at 3 AM without hesitation.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 43 at 12:03, a kid in a dinosaur costume hopped on, didn't even flinch when it jolted. Only in SF do you see kids embracing the chaos in style.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always think 'Gràcia' refers to just Park Güell. They miss the real gems like Carrer de l'Escorial, where the locals actually hang out.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot a recent arrival by their over-reliance on Google Maps for every little detour, even just to grab a café con leche.
